claim: The spine provides structure and support to the body.
source: The spine provides structure and support to the body, yet how it develops its characteristic morphology as the organism grows is little understood.
evidence: This is a general statement about spine function presented in the abstract without specific experimental support in this manuscript.

claim: Scoliosis, kyphosis, and lordosis are conditions in which the spine curves abnormally.
source: This is underscored by the commonality of conditions in which the spine curves abnormally such as scoliosis, kyphosis, and lordosis.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about spinal deformities.

claim: Zebrafish have emerged as promising tools to understand the origin of spinal curves.
source: Recently, zebrafish have emerged as promising tools with which to understand the origin of spinal curves.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation context in the broader manuscript.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 are essential for maintaining spine morphology in zebrafish.
source: Using zebrafish, we demonstrate that the urotensin II-related peptides (URPs), Urp1 and Urp2, are essential for maintaining spine morphology.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing spinal curves in mutants lacking these peptides.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 are 10-amino acid cyclic peptides.
source: Urp1 and Urp2 are 10-amino acid cyclic peptides expressed by neurons lining the central canal of the spinal cord.
evidence: This is supported by the peptide sequence data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 are expressed by neurons lining the central canal of the spinal cord.
source: Urp1 and Urp2 are 10-amino acid cyclic peptides expressed by neurons lining the central canal of the spinal cord.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Combined genetic loss of Urp1 and Urp2 results in adolescent-onset planar curves in the caudal region of the spine.
source: Upon combined genetic loss of Urp1 and Urp2, adolescent-onset planar curves manifested in the caudal region of the spine.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figures 2 and 3 showing curves developing in double mutants.

claim: Urotensin-associated curves occur without vertebral patterning defects.
source: Upon combined genetic loss of Urp1 and Urp2, adolescent-onset planar curves manifested in the caudal region of the spine. Highly similar curves were caused by mutation of Uts2r3, an URP receptor.
evidence: This is supported by calcein staining and µCT analysis in Figure 3 showing normal vertebral patterning.

claim: Mutation of Uts2r3 causes spinal curves similar to those in Urp1/Urp2 double mutants.
source: Highly similar curves were caused by mutation of Uts2r3, an URP receptor.
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2 comparing uts2r3 mutants with urp1/urp2 double mutants.

claim: Urotensin-associated curves are distinct from other zebrafish spinal curve mutants in curve position and direction.
source: Quantitative comparisons revealed that urotensin-associated curves were distinct from other zebrafish spinal curve mutants in curve position and direction.
evidence: This is supported by comparative analysis in Figure 4 showing differences between urotensin mutants and cfap298 mutants.

claim: The Reissner fiber breaks down prior to curve formation in mutants with perturbed cilia motility.
source: Last, we found that the Reissner fiber, a proteinaceous thread that sits in the central canal and has been implicated in the control of spine morphology, breaks down prior to curve formation in mutants with perturbed cilia motility but was unaffected by loss of Uts2r3.
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5 showing RF breakdown in cfap298 mutants.

claim: The Reissner fiber is unaffected by loss of Uts2r3.
source: Last, we found that the Reissner fiber, a proteinaceous thread that sits in the central canal and has been implicated in the control of spine morphology, breaks down prior to curve formation in mutants with perturbed cilia motility but was unaffected by loss of Uts2r3.
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5 showing intact RF in uts2r3 mutants.

claim: Urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit a Reissner fiber-independent mechanism of curvature.
source: This suggests a Reissner fiber-independent mechanism of curvature in urotensin-deficient mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claim: The chordate body axis forms during embryonic development based around the rod-like notochord.
source: The chordate body axis forms during embryonic development, when it is based around the rod-like notochord (Stemple, 2005).
evidence: This is established developmental biology knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The vertebrate axis comprises a column of repeating vertebrae which grows during juvenile and adolescent phases.
source: Later, the vertebrate axis comprises a column of repeating vertebrae which grows during juvenile and adolescent phases and is then maintained during adult life for up to several decades in some species (Bagnat and Gray, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about vertebrate development supported by citation.

claim: Less is known about how spine morphology is maintained during growth and adulthood compared to embryogenesis.
source: While a great deal has been learned about how the body axis emerges during embryogenesis, less is known about how spine morphology is maintained during growth and adulthood.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Scoliosis is medically defined as lateral curvatures of the spine greater than 10°.
source: Scoliosis is medically defined as lateral curvatures of the spine greater than 10° (Cheng et al., 2015; Mesiti, 2021; Wise et al., 2008) and can be caused by congenital defects of vertebral patterning or as a secondary consequence of neuromuscular disease (Pourquié, 2011; Wishart and Kivlehan, 2021).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Scoliosis can be caused by congenital defects of vertebral patterning or as a secondary consequence of neuromuscular disease.
source: Scoliosis is medically defined as lateral curvatures of the spine greater than 10° (Cheng et al., 2015; Mesiti, 2021; Wise et al., 2008) and can be caused by congenital defects of vertebral patterning or as a secondary consequence of neuromuscular disease (Pourquié, 2011; Wishart and Kivlehan, 2021).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Most cases of scoliosis are idiopathic in nature with no known etiology.
source: However, most cases of scoliosis are idiopathic in nature, with no known etiology: approximately 3% of children are afflicted by idiopathic scoliosis, which most often onsets during adolescence (Cheng et al., 2015; Labrom et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Approximately 3% of children are afflicted by idiopathic scoliosis.
source: However, most cases of scoliosis are idiopathic in nature, with no known etiology: approximately 3% of children are afflicted by idiopathic scoliosis, which most often onsets during adolescence (Cheng et al., 2015; Labrom et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statistical fact from the medical literature supported by citations.

claim: Idiopathic scoliosis most often onsets during adolescence.
source: However, most cases of scoliosis are idiopathic in nature, with no known etiology: approximately 3% of children are afflicted by idiopathic scoliosis, which most often onsets during adolescence (Cheng et al., 2015; Labrom et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Kyphosis occurs when there is excessive curvature of the thoracic region of the vertebral column, resulting in a hunched upper back.
source: By contrast, kyphosis and lordosis occur when there is excessive curvature of the thoracic and lumbar regions of the vertebral column, respectively, resulting in a hunched upper back (kyphosis) or a concave lower back (lordosis) (Ogura et al., 2021) without vertebral structural defects.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Lordosis occurs when there is excessive curvature of the lumbar region of the vertebral column, resulting in a concave lower back.
source: By contrast, kyphosis and lordosis occur when there is excessive curvature of the thoracic and lumbar regions of the vertebral column, respectively, resulting in a hunched upper back (kyphosis) or a concave lower back (lordosis) (Ogura et al., 2021) without vertebral structural defects.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Kyphosis and lordosis occur without vertebral structural defects.
source: By contrast, kyphosis and lordosis occur when there is excessive curvature of the thoracic and lumbar regions of the vertebral column, respectively, resulting in a hunched upper back (kyphosis) or a concave lower back (lordosis) (Ogura et al., 2021) without vertebral structural defects.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: There are likely to be overlapping as well as distinct causes of different types of spinal curves.
source: Since these categories of curves can co-occur, there are likely to be overlapping as well as distinct causes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that different curve types can co-occur.

claim: A challenge to understanding the origin of spinal curvature has been the dearth of suitable animal models.
source: A challenge to understanding the origin of spinal curvature has been the dearth of suitable animal models recapitulating disease states.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field.

claim: Zebrafish have emerged as prominent animal models of spinal deformity.
source: Recently, teleost fishes, in particular zebrafish (Danio rerio), have emerged as prominent animal models of spinal deformity (Bagnat and Gray, 2020; Bearce and Grimes, 2021; Boswell and Ciruna, 2017; Gorman and Breden, 2009; Roy, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent literature.

claim: Motile cilia-generated cerebrospinal fluid flow is essential for maintaining body and spine morphology in zebrafish.
source: Using zebrafish, it was found that motile cilia-generated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow is essential for maintaining body and spine morphology (Grimes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Mutants with defective motile cilia failed to undergo axial straightening and developed 'curly tail down' (CTD).
source: Mutants with defective motile cilia failed to undergo axial straightening during embryogenesis and so developed a misshapen early embryonic body axis called 'curly tail down' (CTD; Brand et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: If rescued during the early embryonic stage, cilia motility mutants develop three-dimensional spinal curves that recapitulate features of idiopathic scoliosis.
source: If rescued during this early stage, mutants went on to develop three-dimensional spinal curves that recapitulated some features of idiopathic scoliosis, including adolescent-stage onset in the absence of vertebral patterning defects (Grimes et al., 2016; Marie-Hardy et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cilia motility is essential for the assembly of the Reissner fiber during early larval stages.
source: Precisely how motile cilia and CSF flow maintain spine morphology during growth is not understood, but it is known that during early larval stages cilia motility is essential for the assembly of the Reissner fiber (RF), an extracellular thread-like structure composed predominantly of the large glycoprotein SCOspondin (encoded by sspo) which sits in the CSF in brain ventricles and the central canal (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Rodríguez et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Reissner fiber is an extracellular thread-like structure composed predominantly of the large glycoprotein SCOspondin.
source: Precisely how motile cilia and CSF flow maintain spine morphology during growth is not understood, but it is known that during early larval stages cilia motility is essential for the assembly of the Reissner fiber (RF), an extracellular thread-like structure composed predominantly of the large glycoprotein SCOspondin (encoded by sspo) which sits in the CSF in brain ventricles and the central canal (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Rodríguez et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Zebrafish sspo mutants exhibited CTD as embryos.
source: Zebrafish sspo mutants exhibited CTD as embryos while hypomorphic mutants which can survive beyond embryonic stages also manifested spinal curves (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Hypomorphic sspo mutants that survive beyond embryonic stages manifest spinal curves.
source: Zebrafish sspo mutants exhibited CTD as embryos while hypomorphic mutants which can survive beyond embryonic stages also manifested spinal curves (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 may function downstream of motile cilia in the central canal.
source: The URPs, Urp1 and Urp2, may also function downstream of motile cilia in the central canal.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the relationship between cilia motility and urp expression.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 have been previously linked to heart disease and mental illness.
source: Urp1 and Urp2 are 10-amino acid cyclic peptides previously linked to heart disease and mental illness (Sugo et al., 2003; Konno et al., 2013; Nobata et al., 2011; Parmentier et al., 2011; Quan et al., 2021; Tostivint et al., 2006; Vaudry et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: In zebrafish, Urp1 and Urp2 are expressed in CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs).
source: In zebrafish, Urp1 and Urp2 are expressed in CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs), flow sensory neurons in the central canal, and their expression is increased by motile cilia function and the RF (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Quan et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and by in situ data in Figure 1D.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 expression is increased by motile cilia function and the RF.
source: In zebrafish, Urp1 and Urp2 are expressed in CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs), flow sensory neurons in the central canal, and their expression is increased by motile cilia function and the RF (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Quan et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1F.

claim: Morpholino knockdown of Urp1/Urp2 results in embryonic CTD phenotypes.
source: Morpholino knockdown of Urp1/Urp2 results in embryonic CTD phenotypes while addition of Urp1/Urp2 peptides can rescue the CTD of cilia motility- and RF-deficient mutants (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Addition of Urp1/Urp2 peptides can rescue the CTD of cilia motility- and RF-deficient mutants.
source: Morpholino knockdown of Urp1/Urp2 results in embryonic CTD phenotypes while addition of Urp1/Urp2 peptides can rescue the CTD of cilia motility- and RF-deficient mutants (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 act downstream of cilia motility to promote early axial straightening.
source: This suggested that Urp1 and Urp2 act downstream of cilia motility to promote early axial straightening (Grimes, 2019; Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on previous work, supported by citations.

claim: urp1 and urp2 are 5-exon genes with the final exon coding for the 10-amino acid peptides.
source: Urp1 and Urp2 are encoded by 5-exon genes with the final exon coding for the 10-amino acid peptides that are released by cleavage from the pro-domain (Figure 1A–B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by the gene structure diagrams in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The urp1∆P mutant line lacks the peptide coding sequence.
source: We refer to the resulting mutant lines as urp1∆P and urp2∆P because they lack the peptide coding sequence.
evidence: This is supported by the description of the mutations in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The urp2∆P mutant line lacks the peptide coding sequence.
source: We refer to the resulting mutant lines as urp1∆P and urp2∆P because they lack the peptide coding sequence.
evidence: This is supported by the description of the mutations in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: urp1 and urp2 transcripts are downregulated in urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants, respectively.
source: In addition, mRNA quantitation revealed downregulation of urp1 and urp2 in their respective mutant backgrounds, indicating transcript decay (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 peptides have identical hexacyclic regions.
source: We reasoned that the absence of CTD in urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants might reflect redundancy, since Urp1 and Urp2 peptides are highly similar, with identical hexacyclic regions (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by the peptide sequence data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: urp1∆P and urp2∆P single mutants undergo normal axial straightening.
source: Surprisingly, both urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants underwent normal axial straightening and did not exhibit CTD (Figure 1Ei).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Ei showing straight embryos.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit CTD.
source: By contrast, we observed CTD in both cfap298tm304 mutants that lack cilia motility in the central canal (Bearce et al., 2022) and sspob1446 mutants in which the RF constituent SCOspondin is mutated, as expected (Figure 1Ei, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Ei showing curved embryos.

claim: sspob1446 mutants exhibit CTD.
source: By contrast, we observed CTD in both cfap298tm304 mutants that lack cilia motility in the central canal (Bearce et al., 2022) and sspob1446 mutants in which the RF constituent SCOspondin is mutated, as expected (Figure 1Ei, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Ei showing curved embryos.

claim: cfap298tm304 and sspob1446 mutants maintain urp1 and urp2 expression in CSF-cNs.
source: Notably, cfap298tm304 and sspob1446 mutants maintained urp1 and urp2 expression in CSF-cNs, central canal neurons marked by pkd2l1 expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 1D.

claim: urp1 and urp2 transcripts are quantitatively reduced in cfap298tm304 and sspob1446 mutants.
source: However, urp1 and urp2 transcripts were quantitatively reduced in cfap298tm304 and sspob1446 mutants (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1F.

claim: Maternal zygotic urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants exhibit linear body axes.
source: However, maternal zygotic urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants also exhibited linear body axes (Figure 1Ei), ruling out redundant or maternal gene product function.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Ei showing straight embryos.

claim: cfap298 and sspo crispants exhibit robust CTD.
source: In positive control experiments, cfap298 and sspo crispants exhibited robust CTD, phenocopying germline cfap298tm304 and sspob1446 mutants (Figure 1Eii).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Eii showing curved embryos.

claim: urp1 and urp2 single and double crispants exhibit straight body axes.
source: By contrast, urp1 and urp2 single and double crispants exhibited straight body axes that were not different to uninjected embryos or embryos injected with Cas9 only (Figure 1Eii and H).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and quantitation data in Figure 1Eii and H.

claim: High levels of insertion-deletion mutations were generated at gRNA sites in crispants.
source: Using T7 endonuclease assays, we confirmed that high levels of insertion-deletion mutations were generated at gRNA sites in crispants (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D).
evidence: This is supported by T7E1 assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D.

claim: Normal axial straightening upon mutation of urp1 and urp2 was observed on WIK and TU genetic backgrounds.
source: We used the AB genetic background for the majority of our work, but we also generated and phenotyped urp1;urp2 double crispants on WIK and TU backgrounds to test for potential background effects. Normal axial straightening upon mutation of urp1 and urp2 was also observed on these backgrounds (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitation data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 peptides are dispensable for axial straightening in embryonic zebrafish.
source: We conclude that Urp1 and Urp2 peptides are dispensable for axial straightening in embryonic zebrafish.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation that multiple types of mutants lacking Urp1/Urp2 undergo normal straightening.

claim: urp1∆P mutant adults at 3 months post fertilization appear normal.
source: Outwardly, urp1∆P mutant adults at 3 months post fertilization (mpf) appeared normal whereas urp2∆P mutants exhibited minor body dysmorphologies and kinked tails (n=72 for urp1∆P mutants and n=92 for urp1∆P mutants, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: urp2∆P mutants exhibit minor body dysmorphologies and kinked tails at 3 months post fertilization.
source: Outwardly, urp1∆P mutant adults at 3 months post fertilization (mpf) appeared normal whereas urp2∆P mutants exhibited minor body dysmorphologies and kinked tails (n=72 for urp1∆P mutants and n=92 for urp1∆P mutants, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: urp1∆P mutants exhibit overtly normal skeletal morphology at 3 mpf.
source: Three-dimensional reconstitutions of µCT data from 3 mpf fish showed that urp1∆P mutants indeed exhibited overtly normal skeletal morphology (n=7) while urp2∆P mutants showed slight sagittal curves (n=4; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Figure 2—videos 1–3).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: urp2∆P mutants show slight sagittal curves at 3 mpf.
source: Three-dimensional reconstitutions of µCT data from 3 mpf fish showed that urp1∆P mutants indeed exhibited overtly normal skeletal morphology (n=7) while urp2∆P mutants showed slight sagittal curves (n=4; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Figure 2—videos 1–3).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants exhibit prominent curves with significant dorsal-ventral Cobb angles at 3 mpf.
source: By contrast to these absent or mild deformities in single mutants, urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants exhibited prominent curves, with significant dorsal-ventral Cobb angles, a measure of deviation from straightness, especially in the caudal region of the spine (Figure 2B and D–F, Figure 2—figure supplements 1A and 2A, Figure 2—videos 1–4).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data and Cobb angle measurements in Figure 2.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 function in a semi-redundant fashion in controlling adult spine morphology.
source: These data indicate that Urp1 and Urp2 are essential for adult spine morphology, and that they function in a semi-redundant fashion in this context.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that single mutants have mild or no phenotypes while double mutants have severe phenotypes.

claim: urp1∆P mutants exhibit mild kyphosis-like curves at 12 mpf.
source: At this later time point, urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants exhibited mild kyphosis-like curves though urp2∆P mutants were more severe (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Figure 2—videos 5–7).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: urp2∆P mutants exhibit more severe kyphosis-like curves than urp1∆P mutants at 12 mpf.
source: At this later time point, urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants exhibited mild kyphosis-like curves though urp2∆P mutants were more severe (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Figure 2—videos 5–7).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 are essential for maintenance of spine morphology throughout adulthood and aging.
source: These degenerative phenotypes demonstrate that Urp1 and Urp2 are essential for maintenance of spine morphology throughout adulthood and aging, and suggest that Urp2 plays a larger role than Urp1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that phenotypes worsen with age in single mutants.

claim: Urp2 plays a larger role than Urp1 in maintaining spine morphology.
source: These degenerative phenotypes demonstrate that Urp1 and Urp2 are essential for maintenance of spine morphology throughout adulthood and aging, and suggest that Urp2 plays a larger role than Urp1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that urp2 mutants have more severe phenotypes than urp1 mutants.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 peptides engage G-protein-coupled receptors.
source: Urp1 and Urp2 peptides engage G-protein-coupled receptors (Ames et al., 1999; Chatenet et al., 2004; Elshourbagy et al., 2002; Labarrère et al., 2003; Liu et al., 1999; Nothacker et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: A single urotensin II receptor (UT) gene is found in humans.
source: While a single urotensin II receptor (UT) gene is found in humans and has recently been linked to abnormal spinal curvature (Dai et al., 2021), the zebrafish genome encodes five such receptors.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The human urotensin II receptor has been linked to abnormal spinal curvature.
source: While a single urotensin II receptor (UT) gene is found in humans and has recently been linked to abnormal spinal curvature (Dai et al., 2021), the zebrafish genome encodes five such receptors.
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent work.

claim: The zebrafish genome encodes five urotensin receptors.
source: While a single urotensin II receptor (UT) gene is found in humans and has recently been linked to abnormal spinal curvature (Dai et al., 2021), the zebrafish genome encodes five such receptors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the zebrafish genome.

claim: Uts2r3 was previously implicated in spine morphology.
source: One of those, Uts2r3, was previously implicated in spine morphology (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The uts2r3b1436 mutant line harbors a 178-amino acid deletion after the third amino acid.
source: To systematically compare the effects of Uts2r3 receptor mutation with loss of Urp1 and Urp2, we generated a uts2r3 mutant line harboring a 178-amino acid deletion after the third amino acid, significantly disrupting the protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the mutation description in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants undergo normal axial straightening as embryos.
source: Like urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants, these uts2r3b1436 mutants underwent normal axial straightening as embryos (Figure 1Ei) and went on to exhibit spinal curves as adults (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—video 8).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Ei.

claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants exhibit spinal curves as adults.
source: Like urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants, these uts2r3b1436 mutants underwent normal axial straightening as embryos (Figure 1Ei) and went on to exhibit spinal curves as adults (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—video 8).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2C.

claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants and urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants have similar Cobb angles, though curves in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants are slightly more severe.
source: Cobb angle measurements showed that uts2r3b1436 mutants and urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants were similar, though curves in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants were slightly more severe (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: This is supported by Cobb angle measurements in Figure 2D–E.

claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants show mostly caudally located curves, especially in the most rostral of the caudal vertebrae.
source: Like urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants, uts2r3b1436 mutants showed mostly caudally located curves, especially in the most rostral of the caudal vertebrae (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by curve position data in Figure 2F.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 control spine morphology largely by signaling through Uts2r3.
source: Thus, although we cannot rule out minor roles for other UT receptors, these data suggest that Urp1 and Urp2 control spine morphology largely by signaling through Uts2r3.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of phenotypes between urp1/urp2 double mutants and uts2r3 mutants.

claim: Several types of human spinal curves onset during adolescent growth.
source: Several types of human spinal curves onset during adolescent growth (Cheng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Subtle curves first become apparent in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants between 9 and 11 days post fertilization.
source: Subtle curves first became apparent between 9 and 11 days pf (dpf), corresponding to a standard length between 3.9±0.7 mm and 5.9±0.4 mm (mean ± s.d.; Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—video 1), a stage when adolescents were rapidly growing (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and growth curve data in Figure 3A–C.

claim: Curves are evident in all urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants by 13 dpf.
source: By 13 dpf (standard length 6.2±0.3 mm), curves were evident in all urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants and progressively worsened up to 17 dpf (8.3±0.4 mm) when we ended this analysis (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 3A–B.

claim: At 1 mpf, five of seven urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants exhibit a significant curve in the pre-caudal vertebrae in addition to a caudal curve.
source: At 1 mpf, we assessed urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants by µCT and found variability in curve position and amplitude (Figure 3D). Notably, at this stage, five of seven mutants exhibited a significant curve in the pre-caudal vertebrae, in addition to a caudal curve (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1Ai-Bii).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pre-caudal curves are rare in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants at 3 mpf.
source: Since pre-caudal curves were rare in mutants at 3 mpf (Figure 2B and F), this suggested that curve location is dynamic and that pre-caudal curves form then resolve or shift in some mutants as they grow to adulthood.
evidence: This is supported by curve position data in Figure 2F.

claim: Curve location is dynamic in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants as they grow to adulthood.
source: Since pre-caudal curves were rare in mutants at 3 mpf (Figure 2B and F), this suggested that curve location is dynamic and that pre-caudal curves form then resolve or shift in some mutants as they grow to adulthood.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that pre-caudal curves are common at 1 mpf but rare at 3 mpf.

claim: Calcein staining revealed no defects in vertebral patterning or spacing in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants at 10 dpf.
source: Staining of juveniles with the vital dye calcein revealed no defects in vertebral patterning or spacing in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants at 10 dpf (4.5–6 mm standard length [Figure 3C]) (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by calcein staining data in Figure 3G.

claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants exhibit more variable vertebral length aspect ratios than wild type.
source: Vertebral body length and height aspect ratios were 1.00±0.007 (mean ± s.d.) and 0.99±0.007, respectively, for wild type (n=4; Figure 3F). By contrast, urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants exhibited more variable vertebral length aspect ratios (0.97±0.03, p=0.022; Bartlett's test for equal variances, Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by vertebral morphometry data in Figure 3F.

claim: Vertebral height aspect ratios in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants are not significantly different from controls.
source: Vertebral height aspect ratios in mutants (1.00±0.006) were not significantly different to controls (p=0.745, Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by vertebral morphometry data in Figure 3F.

claim: Small changes in vertebral shape in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants are likely due to the presence of curves rather than causative of curves.
source: These data are consistent with subtle vertebral shape defects at the points of curvature in urp1∆Purp2∆P mutants. However, we do not observe vertebral fusions or missing or transformed appendages, suggesting that vertebral defects do not underlie spinal curves; instead, small changes in vertebral shape are likely due to the presence of curves themselves rather than causative of curves in the first place.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that vertebral defects are subtle and similar to what occurs in non-congenital human scoliosis.

claim: There are no significant differences in curve penetrance or severity between males and females in urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants.
source: Additionally, we parsed our phenotypic data for sex since spinal curves often show sex bias in severity in humans (Cheng et al., 2015), something which has been recapitulated in some zebrafish spinal curve mutants (Marie-Hardy et al., 2021). However, in both urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants, we found no significant differences in curve penetrance or severity between males and females (Figure 2E').
evidence: This is supported by sex-parsed data in Figure 2E'.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit reduced cilia motility in the central canal.
source: The cfap298tm304 line harbors a temperature-sensitive mutation in cfap298, a gene required for cilia motility in several organisms including humans (Austin-Tse et al., 2013; Bearce et al., 2022; Jaffe et al., 2016). cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit reduced cilia motility in the central canal and, if the resulting CTD is embryonically rescued by temperature shifts, develop adolescent-onset spinal curves (Grimes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: If the CTD of cfap298tm304 mutants is embryonically rescued by temperature shifts, they develop adolescent-onset spinal curves.
source: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit reduced cilia motility in the central canal and, if the resulting CTD is embryonically rescued by temperature shifts, develop adolescent-onset spinal curves (Grimes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and by data in Figure 4.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants were argued to model an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)-like condition.
source: These curves were argued to model an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)-like condition (Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—video 1; Grimes et al., 2016; Marie-Hardy et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: urp1 and urp2 transcripts are significantly downregulated in cfap298tm304 mutants.
source: Importantly, both urp1 and urp2 transcripts were significantly downregulated in cfap298tm304 mutants (Figure 1F) suggesting that spinal curves in cfap298tm304 might be the result of reduced Urp1/Urp2 expression.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1F.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants are more severely curved than urp1∆P;urp2∆P or uts2r3b1436 mutants.
source: First, we calculated dorso-ventral Cobb angles, which revealed that cfap298tm304 mutants were more severely curved (average total Cobb angle: 260.4±32.7°) than either urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants (197.5±38.9°) or uts2r3b1436 mutants (146.1±47.4°) (Figure 4E, Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is supported by Cobb angle measurements in Figure 4E.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants show prominent dorsal-ventral curves in both pre-caudal and caudal vertebrae.
source: Second, cfap298tm304 mutants showed prominent dorsal-ventral curves in the pre-caudal as well as caudal vertebrae, a distinct pattern compared with the predominantly caudal curves in urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants (Figure 4A–C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data and curve position analysis in Figure 4 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit significant lateral curvature of the spine, often with spinal twisting.
source: Third, cfap298tm304 mutants exhibited significant lateral curvature of the spine, often with spinal twisting, a hallmark of AIS-like curves (Figure 4Fi–Fii, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by dorsal view µCT data and lateral curvature quantitation in Figure 4Fi–Fii.

claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants show planar curves with very minor or no lateral deviations.
source: By contrast, urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants showed planar curves, with very minor or no lateral deviations (Figure 4Fi–Fii, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by dorsal view µCT data and lateral curvature quantitation in Figure 4Fi–Fii.

claim: Cilia motility mutants and urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit distinct spinal curve phenotypes.
source: These results demonstrated that cilia motility mutants and urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit distinct spinal curve phenotypes.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative differences in curve severity, position, and direction between mutant types.

claim: The causes of spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants can only be partially explained by reduced Urp1/Urp2 expression.
source: As such, the causes of spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants can only be partially explained by reduced Urp1/Urp2 expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cfap298 mutants have more severe and different curves than urotensin-deficient mutants.

claim: cfap298tm304;urp1∆P;urp2∆P triple mutants exhibit significant curves similar to cfap298tm304 single mutants.
source: To further explore the relationship between cilia motility and urotensin peptides, we generated adult cfap298tm304;urp1∆P;urp2∆P triple mutants that were embryonically rescued by temperature shifts. Triple mutants exhibited significant curves, similar to cfap298tm304 single mutants (Figure 4D–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E, Figure 4—video 2; average total Cobb angle: 284.4±33.5°).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data and Cobb angle measurements in Figure 4D–E.

claim: The curves of cfap298tm304;urp1∆P;urp2∆P triple mutants are three-dimensional in nature, with both dorso-ventral and medio-lateral deviations, as well as incidences of spinal torsion.
source: The curves of triple mutants were three-dimensional in nature, with both dorso-ventral and medio-lateral deviations, as well as incidences of spinal torsion (Figure 4Fi–Fii, Figure 4—figure supplement 1); curves were present in both pre-caudal and caudal vertebrae, as opposed to being more restricted to caudal vertebrae in urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 4Fi–Fii and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Motile cilia contribute to urotensin-dependent and urotensin-independent pathways controlling spine morphology.
source: Overall, this suggests that motile cilia contribute to urotensin-dependent and urotensin-independent pathways controlling spine morphology.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that triple mutants have similar phenotypes to cfap298 single mutants.

claim: Pkd2l1 is a polycystin family ion channel expressed in CSF-cNs.
source: Pkd2l1 is a polycystin family ion channel expressed in CSF-cNs, the same cell type which expresses Urp1 and Urp2 (Figure 1D; Quan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation and by in situ data in Figure 1D.

claim: Pkd2l1 is responsible for flow-induced Ca2+ signaling in CSF-cNs.
source: Pkd2l1 is responsible for flow-induced Ca2+ signaling in CSF-cNs (Böhm et al., 2016; Sternberg et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: pkd2l1icm02 mutants exhibit normal early axis development.
source: While pkd2l1icm02 mutants exhibited normal early axis development, they went on to develop mild kyphosis-like curves upon aging (Sternberg et al., 2018), a result we recapitulated after raising pkd2l1icm02 mutants on the same genetic background and under the same conditions as urotensin-deficient mutants for direct comparison (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: pkd2l1icm02 mutants develop mild kyphosis-like curves upon aging.
source: While pkd2l1icm02 mutants exhibited normal early axis development, they went on to develop mild kyphosis-like curves upon aging (Sternberg et al., 2018), a result we recapitulated after raising pkd2l1icm02 mutants on the same genetic background and under the same conditions as urotensin-deficient mutants for direct comparison (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This is supported by citation and by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: pkd2l1icm02 mutants show very subtle curves in the pre-caudal vertebrae and absence of lateral deviation at 12 mpf.
source: Notably, pkd2l1icm02 mutants showed very subtle curves in the pre-caudal vertebrae and absence of lateral deviation at 12 mpf but no obvious curves of any kind at 3 mpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-B, Figure 4—videos 3–4).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: The mild kyphosis-like phenotype of pkd2l1icm02 mutants is highly distinct from urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants.
source: This mild kyphosis-like phenotype was therefore also highly distinct from urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of phenotypes across mutant lines.

claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants develop adolescent-onset curves without significant vertebral structural defects or sex bias.
source: Overall, our phenotypic data show that urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants develop adolescent-onset curves without significant vertebral structural defects or sex bias.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple experiments.

claim: Urotensin pathway mutants most closely reflect a lordosis-like condition.
source: Coupled to the consistently caudal location of curves at 3 mpf as well as the lack of lateral deviation, we suggest that urotensin pathway mutants most closely reflect a lordosis-like condition.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic characteristics of the mutants.

claim: Urotensin mutants are phenotypically distinct from established AIS-like (cfap298tm304) and kyphosis-like (pkd2l1icm02) models.
source: In agreement, urotensin mutants were phenotypically distinct from established AIS-like (cfap298tm304) and kyphosis-like (pkd2l1icm02) models.
evidence: This is a summary of comparative phenotypic analysis.

claim: In sibling controls, Sspo localizes into a Reissner fiber throughout the central canal at 28 hpf.
source: First, we assessed Sspo localization in the central canal of cfap298tm304 mutants at 28 hr pf (hpf). In sibling controls, Sspo localized into an RF throughout the central canal (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5A.

claim: cfap298tm304 mutants raised at restrictive temperatures lack Reissner fiber at 28 hpf.
source: By contrast, cfap298tm304 mutants raised at restrictive temperatures, which exhibited reduced central canal cilia motility and CTD (Figure 1E; Bearce et al., 2022), lacked RF. Instead, Sspo was diffusely localized in the central canal in these mutants (Figure 5B), in agreement with previous work showing that cilia motility is required for RF assembly in embryos (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5B.

claim: Sspo is diffusely localized in the central canal in cfap298tm304 mutants at 28 hpf.
source: By contrast, cfap298tm304 mutants raised at restrictive temperatures, which exhibited reduced central canal cilia motility and CTD (Figure 1E; Bearce et al., 2022), lacked RF. Instead, Sspo was diffusely localized in the central canal in these mutants (Figure 5B), in agreement with previous work showing that cilia motility is required for RF assembly in embryos (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5B.

claim: Sspo is diffuse in temperature upshifted cfap298tm304 mutants at 12 dpf.
source: As in embryos, Sspo localized into a defined RF in the central canal in sibling controls (arrow head in Figure 5D) but was diffuse in temperature upshifted cfap298tm304 mutants, both in mutants that had yet to develop curves and those exhibiting subtle curves (Figure 5E, Figure 5H).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5E.

claim: Cilia motility is required for the initial formation of the Reissner fiber and for its maintenance.
source: This demonstrates (1) that cilia motility is not only required for the initial formation of the RF but also for its maintenance; and (2) breakdown of the RF precedes curve onset in cilia motility-deficient mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF breaks down in cfap298 mutants at 12 dpf before curves form.

claim: Breakdown of the Reissner fiber precedes curve onset in cilia motility-deficient mutants.
source: This demonstrates (1) that cilia motility is not only required for the initial formation of the RF but also for its maintenance; and (2) breakdown of the RF precedes curve onset in cilia motility-deficient mutants.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that RF is disrupted at 12 dpf in cfap298 mutants before curves are fully formed.

claim: Continued cilia motility maintains the Reissner fiber structure, and loss of the RF causes AIS-like curves in cilia motility mutants.
source: This supports a model in which continued cilia motility maintains the RF structure, and loss of the RF causes AIS-like curves to develop in cilia motility mutants.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the temporal relationship between RF breakdown and curve formation.

claim: Sspo localizes normally into the Reissner fiber in the central canal at 28 hpf in uts2r3b1436 mutants.
source: In agreement with that lack of axial straightening phenotype in uts2r3b1436 mutant embryos (Figure 1Ei), we found that Sspo localized normally into the RF in the central canal at 28 hpf in uts2r3b1436 mutants (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5C.

claim: Sspo forms an intact Reissner fiber in uts2r3b1436 mutants at 12 dpf as spinal curves are beginning to manifest.
source: At 12 dpf, as spinal curves were beginning to manifest (Figure 5I), Sspo still formed an intact RF in uts2r3b1436 mutants (arrow head in Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5F.

claim: Urotensin-associated curves are not caused by defective Reissner fiber formation.
source: The fact that RF is present in uts2r3b1436 mutants as curves form suggests that urotensin-associated curves are not caused by defective RF formation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claim: Large central canal cells with the appearance of CSF-cNs become GFP-positive in cfap298tm304 and uts2r3b1436 mutants at 12 dpf.
source: While imaging Sspo-GFP at 12 dpf, we noted that in both cfap298tm304 mutants and uts2r3b1436 mutants, large central canal cells with the appearance of CSF-cNs became GFP-positive (arrows in Figure 5E–F), something we rarely observed in control fish (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5E–F.

claim: CSF-cNs may endocytose Sspo-GFP monomers in cfap298tm304 mutants where the RF has broken down and in uts2r3b1436 mutants where RF is making increasing contacts with CSF-cNs.
source: We suggest that CSF-cNs may endocytose Sspo-GFP monomers in cfap298tm304 mutants where the RF has broken down and in uts2r3b1436 mutants where RF is likely to be making increasing numbers of contacts with CSF-cNs (Orts-Del'Immagine et al., 2020) owing to the onset of spinal curves.
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the observation of GFP-positive CSF-cNs.

claim: Urotensin II (UII) was first identified from the teleost urophysis.
source: Urotensin II (UII) is a cyclic peptide that was first identified from the teleost urophysis (Pearson et al., 1980) and subsequently found to exist in amphibians (Conlon et al., 1992) and mammals (Coulouarn et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Urotensin II was subsequently found to exist in amphibians and mammals.
source: Urotensin II (UII) is a cyclic peptide that was first identified from the teleost urophysis (Pearson et al., 1980) and subsequently found to exist in amphibians (Conlon et al., 1992) and mammals (Coulouarn et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: URP was isolated from the brains of rodents.
source: A highly similar peptide, called URP was then isolated from the brains of rodents (Sugo et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: UII and URP both signal via the UT, a G-protein-coupled receptor.
source: UII and URP both signal via the UT, a G-protein-coupled receptor (Ames et al., 1999; Liu et al., 1999; Mori et al., 1999; Nothacker et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: UIIs, URPs, and UTs have been linked to cardiovascular function and inflammation.
source: UIIs, URPs, and UTs have been linked to cardiovascular function and inflammation, but their roles in the development of morphology are little understood.
evidence: This is general knowledge about urotensin function.

claim: The roles of UIIs, URPs, and UTs in the development of morphology are little understood.
source: UIIs, URPs, and UTs have been linked to cardiovascular function and inflammation, but their roles in the development of morphology are little understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 function semi-redundantly to control spine morphology.
source: In this study, we discovered a role for two of the URPs, Urp1 and Urp2, in zebrafish spine morphology. To do so, we generated urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants that lacked the genetic region coding for the Urp1 and Urp2 peptides, respectively, then phenotyped skeletal morphology by µCT. This revealed that Urp1 and Urp2 function semi-redundantly to control spine morphology, with double mutants, as well as Uts2r3 receptor mutants, developing spinal curves in the caudal region during adolescent growth.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: The lack of major vertebral defects and the location and direction of curves suggest that urotensin-deficient mutants model a lordosis-like condition.
source: The lack of major vertebral defects, the location and direction of the curves coupled with phenotypic differences compared with mutants that model AIS and kyphosis, suggested that urotensin-deficient mutants model a lordosis-like condition.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic characteristics of the mutants.

claim: RF breaks down prior to curve formation in the cilia motility cfap298tm304 mutant.
source: We find that RF breaks down prior to curve formation in the cilia motility cfap298tm304 mutant.
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5.

claim: RF breakdown is a major factor driving spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants.
source: Given other studies linking presence of the RF with a linear body axis, this strongly suggests that RF breakdown is a major factor driving spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal relationship between RF breakdown and curve formation, along with previous studies.

claim: Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibit an intact Reissner fiber.
source: By contrast, Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibited an intact RF, demonstrating that curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants and nor do the presence of curves significantly disrupt RF structure.
evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5.

claim: Curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants.
source: By contrast, Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibited an intact RF, demonstrating that curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants and nor do the presence of curves significantly disrupt RF structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claim: The presence of curves does not significantly disrupt RF structure in urotensin pathway mutants.
source: By contrast, Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibited an intact RF, demonstrating that curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants and nor do the presence of curves significantly disrupt RF structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claim: Urotensin signals act downstream of RF function in controlling spine morphology.
source: This coheres with a model in which urotensin signals act downstream of RF function in controlling spine morphology.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the observation that RF is intact in urotensin mutants and that urp expression is controlled by RF.

claim: urp1 and urp2 expression are controlled by RF function during embryonic phases.
source: Similarly, urp1 and urp2 expression are known to be controlled by RF function during embryonic phases (Figure 1F; Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations and by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1F.

claim: Motile cilia mutants and sspo mutants exhibit three-dimensional spinal curves, with dorso-ventral and medio-lateral curvature.
source: Intriguingly, motile cilia mutants and sspo mutants exhibit three-dimensional spinal curves, with dorso-ventral and medio-lateral curvature (Grimes et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit largely planar curves, only in the dorso-ventral direction.
source: By contrast, we find that urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit largely planar curves, only in the dorso-ventral direction, thereby potentially uncoupling two systems controlling posture (Picton et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by lateral curvature quantitation in Figure 4.

claim: Urp1 is expressed only in ventral CSF-cNs while Urp2 is expressed in both dorsal and ventral CSF-cNs.
source: While Urp1 and Urp2 are co-expressed in ventral CSF-cNs, only Urp2 is expressed in dorsal CSF-cNs (Figure 1D; Quan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 1D and citation.

claim: Dorso-ventral spine shape may be mediated specifically by ventral CSF-cNs which express higher amounts of Urp1/Urp2 peptides.
source: It is therefore tempting to speculate that dorso-ventral spine shape is mediated specifically by ventral CSF-cNs which express higher amounts of Urp1/Urp2 peptides, resulting in dorso-ventral curves in urotensin-deficient mutants.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the expression pattern of urp1 and urp2.

claim: While Urp1/Urp2 expression is in part controlled by upstream cilia motility and RF function, decreased urotensin signaling cannot account fully for the spinal curve phenotypes that occur upon loss of cilia motility or the RF.
source: This also suggests, as above, that while Urp1/Urp2 expression is in part controlled by upstream cilia motility and RF function, decreased urotensin signaling cannot account fully for the spinal curve phenotypes that occur upon loss of cilia motility or the RF.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cfap298 mutants have more severe and different curves than urotensin mutants.

claim: The RF is required for both dorsal and ventral CSF-cN function.
source: Indeed, the RF is required for both dorsal and ventral CSF-cN function (Orts-Del'Immagine et al., 2020), which may explain why dorso-ventral and medio-lateral curves occur when RF is disrupted either by cilia motility mutations or mutations to SCOspondin.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Increased urp1 and urp2 expression occurs upon mutation of rpgrip1l.
source: This scenario is further complicated by the finding that increased urp1 and urp2 expression occurs upon mutation of rpgrip1l, a gene encoding a component of the ciliary transition zone (Vesque et al., 2019 — preprint).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a preprint.

claim: Various cilia-dependent signals likely control the precise levels of Urp1/Urp2 peptides.
source: As such, various cilia-dependent signals likely control the precise levels of Urp1/Urp2 peptides, and controlling those levels appears critical for maintaining the shape of the spine.
evidence: This is inferred from the complex relationship between cilia, RF, and urp expression.

claim: Controlling Urp1/Urp2 peptide levels appears critical for maintaining the shape of the spine.
source: As such, various cilia-dependent signals likely control the precise levels of Urp1/Urp2 peptides, and controlling those levels appears critical for maintaining the shape of the spine.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that loss of Urp1/Urp2 causes spinal curves.

claim: urp1∆P mutants exhibit no obvious phenotypes at 3 mpf but show abnormal curves by 12 mpf.
source: In addition to exhibiting phenotypic differences in terms of curve direction compared with cilia motility and RF mutants, urotensin-deficient mutants also showed gradual worsening of spinal phenotypes upon aging. urp1∆P mutants exhibited no obvious phenotypes at 3 mpf but by 12 mpf showed abnormal curves, while urp2∆P showed mild curves at 3 mpf and more severe deformity at 12 mpf.
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: urp2∆P mutants show mild curves at 3 mpf and more severe deformity at 12 mpf.
source: In addition to exhibiting phenotypic differences in terms of curve direction compared with cilia motility and RF mutants, urotensin-deficient mutants also showed gradual worsening of spinal phenotypes upon aging. urp1∆P mutants exhibited no obvious phenotypes at 3 mpf but by 12 mpf showed abnormal curves, while urp2∆P showed mild curves at 3 mpf and more severe deformity at 12 mpf.
evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Urp1/Urp2 function throughout adulthood and aging to maintain spine morphology.
source: This implies that Urp1/Urp2 function throughout adulthood and aging to maintain spine morphology.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that phenotypes worsen with age in single mutants.

claim: Partial redundancy between Urp1 and Urp2 occurs while overall dose likely sets how early phenotypes manifest.
source: Since double mutants were more severe at 3 mpf than either single mutant, partial redundancy between Urp1 and Urp2 appears to occur while overall dose likely sets how early phenotypes manifest.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of single and double mutant phenotypes.

claim: Temperature-shift experiments show no role for motile cilia beyond 34 dpf in maintaining the spine.
source: In contrast to this long-term role for urotensin peptides, temperature-shift experiments in which motile cilia were inactivated after 34 dpf showed no role for motile cilia beyond this stage in maintaining the spine (Grimes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: It has not been determined if motile cilia are required for CSF flow or RF formation in adult fish.
source: It is worth noting, however, that this result does not preclude a role for CSF flow or the RF during long-term spine morphostasis because it has not been determined if motile cilia are required for CSF flow or RF formation in adult fish.
evidence: This is a statement about what is not known.

claim: The spines of humans and zebrafish are broadly similar.
source: The spines of humans and zebrafish are broadly similar, and it has been suggested that spinal loads are comparable (Gorman and Breden, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Zebrafish spines seem predisposed to curvature, with high levels of scoliosis-like curves naturally developing with age.
source: Moreover, zebrafish spines, like human spines, seem predisposed to curvature, with high levels of scoliosis-like curves naturally developing with age (Bearce and Grimes, 2021; Gorman and Breden, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The overall shape of the zebrafish spine is similar to human, with a natural kyphotic curve in the pre-caudal vertebrae and a compensatory lordotic curve in the most anterior caudal vertebrae.
source: The overall shape of the zebrafish spine is also similar to human, with a natural kyphotic curve in the pre-caudal (rib-bearing) vertebrae and a compensatory, albeit very minor, lordotic curve in the most anterior caudal vertebrae.
evidence: This is a comparative anatomical observation.

claim: Zebrafish curves are not as pronounced as in humans.
source: However, these curves are not as pronounced as in humans.
evidence: This is a comparative anatomical observation.

claim: Zebrafish exhibit some fish-specific structures such as the Weberian apparatus.
source: Moreover, zebrafish also exhibit some fish-specific structures such as the Weberian apparatus (Dietrich et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Zebrafish cilia motility mutants appear to model several features of AIS including three-dimensional curves, lack of vertebral patterning defects, adolescent-onset, and sex bias.
source: Nevertheless, zebrafish cilia motility mutants appear to model several features of AIS including the three-dimensional nature of curves, lack of vertebral patterning defects or significant vertebral structural malformations, adolescent-onset and, in some cases, sex bias (Grimes et al., 2016; Marie-Hardy et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The curves of urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants display some features of AIS but are not three-dimensional.
source: The curves of urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants display some of these features as well but, importantly, are not three-dimensional.
evidence: This is supported by lateral curvature quantitation in Figure 4.

claim: Urotensin pathway-deficient mutants display primarily planar curves with little or no lateral deviation, similar to hyper-kyphosis and hyper-lordosis in humans.
source: Instead, urotensin pathway-deficient mutants display primarily planar curves, with little or no lateral deviation. This is more similar to what occurs in hyper-kyphosis and hyper-lordosis in humans, when natural curves are accentuated.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic characteristics of the mutants and comparison to human conditions.

claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants model some aspects of lordosis.
source: Given this planarity, and since curves are mostly present in the caudal vertebrae, we suggest that urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants model some aspects of lordosis and so refer to this phenotype as lordosis-like.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic characteristics of the mutants.

claim: Human lumbar vertebrae and zebrafish caudal vertebrae are structurally distinct.
source: However, we note that human lumbar vertebrae and zebrafish caudal vertebrae are structurally distinct (Boswell and Ciruna, 2017), and humans have a significant natural lordotic curve that allows for an efficient upright walking gait, whereas zebrafish do not.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Urotensin-deficient mutants recapitulate some aspects of lordosis but cannot mimic human-specific aspects of hyper-lordotic curves.
source: Thus, urotensin-deficient mutants recapitulate some aspects of lordosis but clearly cannot mimic human-specific aspects of hyper-lordotic curves.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical differences between zebrafish and humans.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 peptides are genetically dispensable for embryonic axial straightening.
source: A surprising finding from our work was that Urp1 and Urp2 peptides are genetically dispensable for embryonic axial straightening.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data showing normal straightening in mutants lacking Urp1/Urp2.

claim: Morpholino knockdown of Urp1/Urp2 results in failure of axial straightening in some individuals.
source: This interpretation is challenged by morpholino knockdown of Urp1/Urp2, which does result in failure of axial straightening in some individuals, resulting in a CTD phenotype (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The CTD of Urp1/Urp2 morphants is unlikely to result from morpholino off-target effects.
source: One possibility is that the CTD of morphants results from morpholino off-target effects. However, this seems unlikely for three reasons: (1) adding exogenous Urp1/Urp2 peptides to the central canal can rescue the CTD phenotype of cilia motility- and RF-deficient mutants (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018), suggesting the involvement of Urp1/Urp2 in axial straightening, at least in gain-of-function experiments; (2) since motile cilia and the RF are required for both axial straightening during embryogenesis and for the maintenance of spine morphology during adolescence, it seems parsimonious that Urp1/Urp2 peptides would also function across these two life stages; and (3) urp1 and urp2 transcript levels are reduced in motile cilia and RF mutants (Figure 1F; Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018), suggestive of a link between Urp1 and Urp2 upregulation and axial straightening.
evidence: This is argued based on multiple lines of evidence from previous work and this study.

claim: The lack of CTD in urp1/urp2 mutants strongly argues that Urp1 and Urp2 are dispensable for straightening.
source: Nevertheless, the lack of CTD in our mutants, in which the Urp1 and Urp2 peptide coding sequences were entirely removed, is clear: single, double, and maternal-zygotic urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants all underwent normal axial straightening. This strongly argues that Urp1 and Urp2 are dispensable for straightening.
evidence: This is based on the observation that multiple types of mutants lacking Urp1/Urp2 undergo normal straightening.

claim: It is unlikely that the pro-domain sequences of Urp1 and Urp2 are required for straightening.
source: Since the deletions were induced toward the end of the protein, it does leave open the possibility that the pro-domain sequences are required for straightening. However, this seems unlikely for three reasons: (1) urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants showed urp1 and urp2 transcript downregulation, respectively, in addition to deletion of the peptide coding regions; (2) urp1 and urp2 single and double crispants, in which gRNAs targeted several regions of the gene, also showed normal straightening; and (3) exogenous addition of Urp1 and Urp2 peptides, without pro-domains, rescued CTD of a cilia motility and RF mutant (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018), suggesting that it is the peptide itself and not some other region which is functional.
evidence: This is argued based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Genetic compensation may explain the mutant/morphant phenotypic differences.
source: One possibility is that genetic compensation explains the mutant/morphant phenotypic differences (Rossi et al., 2015; Sztal and Stainier, 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the discrepancy, supported by citations to work on genetic compensation.

claim: Transcriptional adaptation is a compensation mechanism in which mutant mRNA decay products promote transcriptional upregulation of genes with similar sequences.
source: A recently discovered compensation mechanism is transcriptional adaptation in which mutant mRNA is decayed and the products of that decay are, via a sequence-dependent mechanism, recruited to genes with similar sequences where they promote transcriptional upregulation (El-Brolosy et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about genetic compensation mechanisms supported by citations.

claim: Slight upregulation of urp2 in urp1∆P mutants may indicate transcriptional adaptation.
source: We did find slight upregulation of urp2 in urp1∆P mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E), which may indicate transcriptional adaptation, although this alone cannot explain the lack of CTD phenotypes in urp1∆P mutants because urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants also lacked CTD.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: A complementary study found that Urp1 and Urp2 function redundantly to maintain spine shape.
source: While we were in the final stages of preparing this manuscript, a study was released which made several complementary findings, also concluding that Urp1 and Urp2 function redundantly to maintain spine shape (Gaillard et al., 2022 — preprint).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a preprint.

claim: Gaillard and colleagues observed no embryonic axial defects upon genetic loss of Urp1 and Urp2.
source: Importantly, and in agreement with our work, Gaillard and colleagues observed no embryonic axial defects upon genetic loss of Urp1 and Urp2.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a preprint.

claim: Other urotensin II-encoding genes are not upregulated in urp1 and urp2 mutants.
source: Moreover, they found that other urotensin II-encoding genes were not upregulated in urp1 and urp2 mutants, arguing against phenotypic masking by genetic compensation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a preprint.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 are not essential for axial straightening during embryogenesis but are required for maintenance of the body axis during growth and adulthood.
source: Our findings and those of Gaillard and colleagues together therefore strongly argue that Urp1 and Urp2 are not essential for axial straightening during embryogenesis but are instead required for the maintenance of the body axis during growth and adulthood.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on findings from this study and a complementary study.

claim: Other mechanisms, currently unknown, likely operate downstream of cilia motility and RF function to mediate embryonic axial straightening.
source: As such, other mechanisms, currently unknown, likely operate downstream of cilia motility and RF function to mediate embryonic axial straightening.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Urp1/Urp2 are not required for straightening despite being downstream of cilia and RF.

claim: Future efforts will be required to discern which tissues respond to Urp1/Urp2 signals during the control of spine morphology.
source: Future efforts will be required to discern which tissues respond to Urp1/Urp2 signals during the control of spine morphology.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: During embryonic stages, Uts2r3 is expressed in dorsal muscle.
source: During embryonic stages, Uts2r3 is expressed in dorsal muscle (Zhang et al., 2018), but it remains unclear how Urp1/Urp2 peptides released by CSF-cNs could signal to effect muscle during adolescent stages.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Based on single-cell RNA-sequencing gene expression atlases, uts2r3 is expressed in several cell types in addition to muscle.
source: Moreover, based on single-cell RNA-sequencing gene expression atlases (Farnsworth et al., 2020), uts2r3 is expressed in several other cell types in addition to muscle.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a gene expression atlas.

claim: It will be critical to determine the timing of action of urotensin signaling.
source: It will also be critical to determine the timing of action of urotensin signaling.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The underlying defect in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants may be caused by an earlier event which only phenotypically manifests later.
source: While we observe phenotypes first appearing between 9 and 11 dpf in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants, it is possible that the underlying defect in mutants is caused by an earlier event which only phenotypically manifests later.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the timing of the defect.

claim: Subtle disruptions to the notochord may later result in spinal curves.
source: One candidate is subtle disruptions to the notochord, which may later result in spinal curves (Bagwell et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citation.

claim: Experiments in which urp1∆P and urp2∆P single mutants were aged argue that Urp1 and Urp2 peptides function throughout life to maintain spine morphology.
source: On the other hand, our experiments in which we aged urp1∆P and urp2∆P single mutants argue that Urp1 and Urp2 peptides function throughout life, and not only during early growth, to maintain spine morphology.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that phenotypes worsen with age in single mutants.

claim: In Xenopus laevis, disruption of Utr4 causes abnormal curvature of the body axis.
source: First, in the frog Xenopus laevis, disruption of Utr4, a counterpart of Uts2r3, causes abnormal curvature of the body axis (Alejevski et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Rare mutations in UTS2R are significantly associated with spinal curvature in AIS patient cohorts.
source: Second, a human genetics study reported that rare mutations in UTS2R are significantly associated with spinal curvature, being discovered within AIS patient cohorts (Dai et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a human genetics study.

claim: A deeper understanding of urotensin signaling in maintaining spine shape will provide insight into principles of morphogenesis and potentially human disease.
source: Thus, a deeper understanding of the role of urotensin signaling in maintaining spine shape will not only provide insight into principles of morphogenesis but potentially also human disease.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the significance of the work.
